   410	\begin{lemma}
   411	  \label{lem:commutation-analysis}
   412	  Let $\{A^x_{a,\, b}\}$, $\{B^x_{a,\, b,\, c}\}$, $\{C^x_{a,\, c}\}$ be POVMs.
   413	  Suppose $\{B^x_{a,\, b,\, c}\}$ is projective, and
   414	  \begin{align*}
   415	    A^x_{a,\, b} \otimes \Id_\bob &\approx_\delta \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, b}\;,\\
   416	    C^x_{a,\, c} \otimes \Id_\bob &\approx_\delta \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, c}\;,
   417	  \end{align*}
   418		where recall that $B^x_{a,\, b} = \sum_c B^x_{a,b,c}$ and similarly $B^x_{a,\, c}=\sum_b B^x_{a,b,c}$. 
   419	  Then the following approximate commutation relation holds:
   420	  \begin{equation*}
   421	    [A^x_{a,\, b}, C^x_{a,\, c}] \otimes I_\bob \approx_\delta 0\;.
   422	  \end{equation*}
   423	\end{lemma}
   424	
   425	\begin{proof}
   426	  Applying Fact~\ref{fact:add-a-proj} to $C^x_{a,\, c} \otimes \Id_\bob
   427	  \approx_\delta \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, c}$ and $\{A^x_{a,b} \otimes
   428	  \Id_\bob \}$, we have
   429	  \begin{equation}
   430	    \label{eq:commutation-analysis-1}
   431	    A^x_{a,\, b} C^x_{a,\, c} \otimes \Id_\bob
   432	    \approx_\delta A^x_{a,\, b} \otimes B^x_{a,\, c}\,.
   433	  \end{equation}
   434	  Similarly, applying Fact~\ref{fact:add-a-proj} to $A^x_{a,\, b} \otimes
   435	  \Id_\bob \approx_\delta \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, b}$ and $\{\Id_\alice
   436	  \otimes B^x_{a,c}\}$, and using the fact that $\{B^x_{a,b,c}\}$ is projective,
   437	  we have
   438	  \begin{equation}
   439	    \label{eq:commutation-analysis-2}
   440	    \begin{split}
   441	      A^x_{a,\, b} \otimes B^x_{a,\, c}
   442	      & \approx_\delta \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, c} B^x_{a,\, b}\\
   443	      & =_{\phantom{\delta}} \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, b,\, c}\,.
   444	    \end{split}
   445	  \end{equation}
   446	  Combining Equations~\eqref{eq:commutation-analysis-1}
   447	  and~\eqref{eq:commutation-analysis-2}, we have
   448	  \begin{equation}
   449	    \label{eq:commutation-analysis-3}
   450	    A^x_{a,\, b} C^x_{a,\, c} \otimes \Id_\bob \approx_\delta
   451	    \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, b,\, c}\,.
   452	  \end{equation}

   454	  \begin{equation}
   455	    \label{eq:commutation-analysis-4}

   457	    \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, b,\, c}\,.

   460	  and~\eqref{eq:commutation-analysis-4}.
   461	\end{proof}

blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:292:The Pauli basis test is the quantum low individual degree test of Natarajan and Vidick, in the slightly modified form introduced by Natarajan and Wright~\cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}. Most subtests probe limited information about $h$: given a point $u_W \in \F_q^m$, a player is expected to report the evaluation $g_h(u_W)$ of the low-degree encoding $g_h$ of $h$, and for a fixed basis $W$ these probes are checked against each other by the classical low individual degree game of Section~\ref{sec:ld-verifier}. Consistency \emph{between} the two bases is checked through two-outcome probes: given additionally $r_W \in \F_q$, a player reports $\tr(g_h(u_W)\, r_W) \in \F_2$. The two binary measurements obtained in this way for $W = X$ and $W = Z$ either commute or anticommute, according to the value $\gamma \in \F_2$ of Equation~\eqref{eq:gamma-value} below. This is the **single\nsource of truth** for agent conventions. Claude Code agents should also read\n`CLAUDE.md` for Claude-specific notes.\n\n## Project Overview\n\nThis repository is a Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization project for mathematics\naround $MIP^* = RE$. It is the **local-only continuation** of\n[LionSR/MIPStarRE](https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE): the inherited track is\nthe **low individual degree test (LDT)** paper (arXiv:2009.12982); the active\ntrack is the **quantum Pauli basis test (QPBT)** from *MIP\\*=RE*\n(arXiv:2001.04383, primary) and *NEEXP in MIP\\** (arXiv:1904.05870, secondary).\n\nGitHub is the authority for active issues and pull requests. Read\n`local/README.md` and `local/DESIGN.md` before workflow actions.\n\nKey locations:\n\n- `references/qpbt-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of MIP\\*=RE\n  (arXiv:2001.04383); the QPBT lives in\n  `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex` and\n  `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex`\n- `references/neexp-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of NEEXP in MIP\\*\n  (arXiv:1904.05870); secondary source\n  (`07_a_self_test_for_the_pauli_basis.tex`)\n- `references/ldt-paper/` — in-repo TeX source mirror for LDT\n- `blueprint/src/` — active LaTeX blueprint with Lean cross-references\n  (`\\lean{}`, `\\leanok`)\n- `MIPStarRE/` — Lean codebase matching the blueprint\n- `audits/` — dated audit reports, scouting notes, and repair plans\n- `local/`, `results/telemetry/` — local execution and research telemetry\n\nA legacy 2111 tensor track exists under `blueprint/legacy/` — do not modify it.\n\n**Canonical source hierarchy** (use in this order):\n\n1. `references/` paper mirrors — TeX source of the papers\n2. `blueprint/src/chapter/` — active LaTeX blueprint\n3. `MIPStarRE/` — Lean scaffold\n\nAlways read the paper source before formalizing or proving a statement. The\npaper contains the precise mathematical definitions, theorem statements, and\nproof strategies that the Lean code must faithfully represent. When stuck on a\nsorry site or proof, go back to the original paper TeX source — the answer is\nalmost always there. Do not guess or try random tactics without first\nunderstanding the paper's proof strategy.\n\n## Repository Layout\n\n```\nMIPStarRE/\n├── Quantum/               # Reusable matrix / measurement infrastructure\n│   ├── FiniteMatrix.lean  # Op d, normalizedTrace, tauNormSq, IsProj, ...\n│   └── Measurement.lean   # POVM, measurement types\n└── LDT/                   # Low individual degree test (13 submodules)\n    ├── Basic/             # Parameters, operators, distributions, submeasurements\n    ├── Test/              # Test definitions & main theorem\n    ├── Preliminaries/\n    ├── MakingMeasurementsProjective/\n    ├── MainInductionStep/\n    ├── ExpansionHypercubeGraph/\n    ├── GlobalVariance/\n    ├── SelfImprovement/\n    ├── CommutativityPoints/\n    ├── Commutativity/\n    └── Pasting/\n```\n\nEach LDT submodule typically has `Defs.lean` and `Theorems.lean`. Root imports\nflow: `MIPStarRE.lean` → `Quantum` + `LDT` → all submodules.\n\n## Quick Start — Build and Check Commands\n\nRun commands from the repository root unless noted otherwise.\n\n### First-time setup\n\n```bash\nlake exe cache get\nlake build\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check\n```\n\nRun the hook check in every fresh worktree before preparing a PR.  The hooks\nmove fast statement-integrity, proof-debt, changed-file Lean, and blueprint-sync\nchecks to the local workflow so CI is not spent on preventable statement drift.\n\n### Full project build (CI-equivalent)\n\n```bash\nlake build\n```\n\n### Fast single-file type-check (default iteration loop)\n\n```bash\nlake env lean MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in one file\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean || true\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in the whole project\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE\n```\n\n### Declaration checker\n\n```bash\nlake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls\n```\n\nUse this when blueprint declaration lists need to match Lean declarations.\n\n### Blueprint build\n\n```bash\nleanblueprint pdf    # PDF output\nleanblueprint web    # HTML output (use as default for quick checks)\n```\n\nIn CI, blueprint linting effectively runs `leanblueprint web` from `blueprint/`.\n\n### What counts as a single test\n\nThis repository does not have a conventional unit-test suite. The closest\nsingle-test commands are:\n\n- **Lean work**: `lake env lean path/to/File.lean` and\n  `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\" path/to/File.lean || true`\n- **Blueprint work**: `leanblueprint web`\n- **Whole-repo verification**: `lake build` and\n  `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\n\n### Recommended validation sequence\n\nFor a Lean file change:\n\n1. Type-check the edited file with `lake env lean ...`\n2. Scan that file for `sorry|axiom`\n3. If the change affects imports or shared declarations, run `lake build`\n\nFor blueprint changes:\n\n1. Run `leanblueprint web`\n2. If declaration links changed, run `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\n\n## Toolchain\n\n- **Lean**: v4.31.0 (from `lean-toolchain`)\n- **Mathlib**: v4.31.0 (from `lakefile.toml`)\n\nImportant `lakefile.toml` options:\n\n- `relaxedAutoImplicit = false` — declare all variables explicitly\n- `pp.unicode.fun = true`\n- `weak.linter.mathlibStandardSet = true`\n- `maxSynthPendingDepth = 3`\n\n## Proof-Filling Order\n\nSections must be filled in this dependency order:\n\n1. Sections 3–4: test setup and preliminaries\n2. Section 5: making measurements projective\n3. Sections 7–8: expansion and global variance\n4. Section 9: self-improvement\n5. Sections 10–11: commutativity\n6. Section 12: pasting\n7. Section 6: main induction wrapper\n\nDo not start from the final theorem and guess intermediate facts.\n\n## Faithful Formalization Policy\n\nA declaration is a formalization of a paper theorem only when its public Lean\nstatement matches the cited paper statement, up to faithful formal encoding.\nChanging a Lean theorem away from the corresponding statement in\n`references/ldt-paper/` is strongly discouraged and should occur only when a\nfaithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical necessity requires it.\nThis applies to every declaration advertised as a formalization of a paper\nresult, not only to theorems currently undergoing repair.  The check is on the\nhypotheses as well as the conclusion.  A theorem whose\nconclusion has the right shape but whose assumptions include an extra\nload-bearing bridge input or hypotheses bundle is a conditional theorem, not\nthe paper theorem.\nThe project goal is to eliminate such conditional bridges, not to normalize\nthem as permanent infrastructure.\n\nIf the only available Lean theorem has extra assumptions, the blueprint must\nnot mark the source-labelled paper entry as matched by that theorem.  Either\nleave the source-labelled entry without `\\leanok`, or state the restricted or\nconditional result as a separate Lean-only blueprint entry whose hypotheses are\ndisplayed explicitly.  A scope-restricted theorem may be marked `\\leanok` only\nagainst a blueprint statement that explicitly states the restriction; it must\nnot be presented as the unrestricted source theorem.\n\nWhen a stricter-hypothesis Lean theorem is the only available version near a\nsource theorem, the discrepancy must have a paper-gap note or tracking issue.\nThe note should identify the missing hypothesis, explain why it is not part of\nthe cited statement, and state the plan for eliminating the restriction,\nderiving it internally, or moving the result out of the source-labelled route.\n\nThis rule applies especially to declarations named after paper labels such as\n`mainFormal`, `selfImprovement`, `mainInduction`, or other theorem names linked\nfrom the blueprint by `\\lean{...}` and `\\leanok`.\n\nBefore editing any theorem tagged with a paper label (`thm:*`, `lem:*`,\n`prop:*`):\n\n1. Read the corresponding statement in `references/ldt-paper/`.\n2. Preserve the public Lean theorem statement, except for hypotheses that are\n   genuinely part of the faithful encoding of the paper's domain.\n3. Do not add bridge inputs, residual packages, repair hypotheses, producer\n   assumptions, generic hypotheses or assumptions bundles, or arbitrary\n   implication hypotheses to the paper theorem.\n4. If a missing intermediate fact is needed, first state that fact as a named\n   lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.\n5. Do not add a conditional helper merely to keep a file compiling.  A\n   conditional helper may remain temporarily only when the proof content it\n   preserves is mathematically useful, the source-faithful theorem remains\n   visible, and the helper has a paper-gap note, a named construction theorem\n   or proof-obligation target, and an explicit discharge or deletion plan.  Its\n   name must show that it is conditional without making the assumption look like\n   an acceptable source hypothesis, for example\n   `mainFormal_ofInternalObligations`, `selfImprovementFromObligations`, or a\n   name ending in `_ofObligations`.\n6. Do not point a source-labelled blueprint theorem to the conditional helper\n   with `\\leanok`.\n\nWhen reviewing an existing bridge, residual, repair, producer, or package\nhypothesis, first try to recover any genuine proof content from its construction\nand turn that content into a source-faithful lemma.  If the bridge does not\nactually follow from the paper hypotheses, do not preserve the paper theorem as\na strengthened statement.  Restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave\nthe missing proof obligation explicit, even if that means reintroducing a\ntracked `sorry` during a repair PR.\n\nSome side conditions are not deviations: positivity needed to define a\ndivision, nonemptiness of a finite type, decidability instances, field-model\ninstances, and similar boundary hypotheses may be faithful encodings of\nassumptions that the paper leaves implicit.  These should still be reviewed and\ndocumented if they are mathematically load-bearing. These assumptions\nshould not be introduced merely to keep a file compiling or to avoid a `sorry`;\nthey require explicit mathematical justification and a planned discharge.\n\nFor the current LDT final theorem, `mainFormal` is reserved for the statement of\n`\\Cref{thm:main-formal}`: from a projective strategy passing the low individual\ndegree test, it produces the three final consistency conclusions.  A theorem\nwith an extra hypothesis such as\n`hbaseBridge : ... → MainFormalRepairedBridgeHypotheses ...` is temporary\nscaffolding at best; it must not be the declaration advertised as\n`thm:main-formal`.  The corresponding paper-aligned version should remain\nvisible, even if its proof is temporarily unfinished during repair.\n\nEvery agent changing a paper-labelled theorem must finish with a statement\nintegrity audit:\n\n- paper assumptions;\n- Lean assumptions;\n- paper conclusion;\n- Lean conclusion;\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\n\n### Paper-realignment mode\n\nWhen a theorem, definition, or hypothesis field has already drifted away from\n`references/ldt-paper/`, a repair PR may temporarily reintroduce `sorry` in\norder to restore the source-faithful statement.  In this mode, statement\nfaithfulness is the first invariant: keeping a divergent proof intact merely to\navoid `sorry` preserves a theorem that the paper does not state.\n\nPaper-realignment mode is narrow.  It applies only to edits whose purpose is to\nremove wrong hypotheses, delete divergent fields, restore a paper theorem\nstatement, or replace a conditional theorem by a paper-facing statement plus a\nnamed proof obligation.  Such a PR must:\n\n1. cite the paper passage by label or line range in the relevant docstring;\n2. cite the paper-gap note or tracking issue that records the divergence;\n3. identify every introduced or retained `sorry` and the construction theorem,\n   proof-obligation theorem, or source-faithful lemma expected to discharge it;\n4. avoid unrelated refactors, notation changes, or proof-engineering churn.\n\nDuring paper realignment, every restated definition, hypothesis field, or\npaper-facing theorem must have a docstring that lets a reviewer tell whether\nthe statement is present in the paper or is a Lean-only proof obligation.  A\nname such as `Bridge`, `Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Input`, or `Producer`\nis not by itself a mathematical source citation.\n\n### Unfaithful dependency markers\n\nA theorem or lemma is **unfaithful** when its proof relies on a hypothesis,\nhelper, bridge, residual, repair input, or conditional theorem that is known not\nto follow from the cited paper statement.  This includes the case where the\npublic theorem statement is source-shaped but the proof calls a conditional\nhelper whose load-bearing hypothesis is not yet derived from the paper\nhypotheses.\n\nSuch a declaration must carry a docstring section beginning with\n`**Unfaithful:**`.  The marker must name the load-bearing deviation, cite the\npaper-gap note or issue that documents it, and state the planned discharge.  A\nminimal form is:\n\n```text\n**Unfaithful:** This proof currently relies on `<hypothesis or helper>`,\nwhich is not derived from `<paper label or line range>`.  Documented in\n`docs/paper-gaps/<note>.tex` or issue `#N`.  Elimination: prove\n`<construction theorem>` from the paper hypotheses.\n```\n\nThe marker propagates through dependencies: a theorem whose proof transitively\nuses an unfaithful declaration is itself unfaithful until the dependency is\nreplaced by a source-faithful proof.  Remove the marker only when the cited\ndeviation has been discharged.\n\nNot every discrepancy requires the full `**Unfaithful:**` marker.  If the paper\nhas a local typo, a documented numerical strengthening, or a genuine scope\nrestriction, use a lighter docstring marker such as `**Local fix:**` or\n`**Scope restriction:**`, citing the relevant paper-gap note.  These lighter\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\npaper hypotheses.\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Imports\n\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\n- One import per line\n- Follow existing local import style\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\n\n### File structure\n\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\n\n1. imports\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\n3. namespace / opens / variables\n4. declarations\n\n### Formatting\n\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\n  own line\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\n  theorem statement\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\n  tactic blocks.\n\n### Naming conventions\n\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\n\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\n\nProject-preferred variable names:\n\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\n- `σ` — strategies\n- `P` — projective measurements\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\n\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\n\n### Types and signatures\n\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\n  wrappers\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\n\n### Documentation\n\nRequired:\n\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\n\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\lean{...}`\nand `\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\n\n## Proof Engineering\n\n### Search before proving\n\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\n\n### Mathlib integration\n\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. When proving lemmas:\n\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\n\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\n\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\n\n### Validation ladder\n\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\n2. `lake build`\n\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\n\n### Lean-specific advice\n\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\n  already in the repo\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\n\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\n\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. Prefer a\nclear, precise, and unhurried expository style: introduce the object under\ndiscussion, state the mathematical relation being used, distinguish hypotheses\nfrom conclusions, and avoid informal process language when a standard\nmathematical phrase is available.\n\nWhen writing docstrings, audit notes, PR descriptions, or blueprint-adjacent\ncomments, use terminology from the standard mathematical literature, the LDT\npaper, and the local formalization. Do not invent slang or private shorthand for\nmathematical objects. The goal is prose that a third-party reader can understand\nwithout having read the agent conversation that produced the change.\n\n### Paper-gap notes\n\nFor the proof-gap terminology used to distinguish source theorems, internal\nproof obligations, and conditional helpers, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.  For documentation of discrepancies\nbetween the cited paper, the blueprint, and Lean, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex`. In particular, such notes should be\nmathematical prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists who have not\nread the issue discussion: introduce notation, state the cited assertion,\nisolate the calculation or logical obstruction, compare with the blueprint and\nLean statement, and give a clear verdict. If Lean uses a Mathlib result or\nconstruction not present in the cited argument, explain that replacement\npedagogically before naming the formal declaration. If the cited assertion is\nfalse and a counterexample is available, explain the counterexample in prose and\nuse any Lean declaration only as verification.\n\n## Proof Integrity\n\n### Blockers (must be resolved before merge)\n\nSee the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md` for the full catalog.\n\n**Direct proof holes**: `sorry`, `admit`\n\n**Kernel / type system bypasses**: `native_decide`, `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce`,\n`lcProof`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`\n\n**Axiom smuggling**: unjustified `axiom` declarations\n\n**Circular reasoning**: proofs that assume the statement being proved as a local\nhypothesis, or helper lemmas that essentially restate the main goal.\n\n**Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)**: custom re-declarations of standard\nMathlib lemmas; `axiom` or `sorry`-based helpers for facts already in Mathlib;\nchains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core.\n\n**Scaffolding that blocks real formalization**: definitions or theorem statements\nthat do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics, making them impossible\nto connect to real Mathlib-based proofs. Ask: *Can a real proof be built on top\nof this?*\n\n### Warnings\n\nPlaceholder tactics (`exact?`, `apply?`, `library_search`) should be replaced\nwith concrete results. Reviewers should consult this file alongside\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md`.\n\n## PR and Commit Conventions\n\nGitHub PRs are opened by `local/bin/pr_open.py` and merged through the guarded\n`local/bin/pr_merge.py` gate. `#N` in PR bodies and commit messages is a GitHub\nissue or PR number. Titles, bodies, and commit rules remain unchanged.\n\n### PR title format\n\n```\ntype(scope): short description\n```\n\n| Type       | When to use                                      |\n|------------|--------------------------------------------------|\n| `feat`     | New definition, lemma, theorem, or module         |\n| `fix`      | Bug fix (broken proof, wrong identifier, etc.)    |\n| `refactor` | Restructuring without changing API surface        |\n| `docs`     | Documentation or blueprint changes only           |\n| `style`    | Formatting, naming, or docstring cleanup only     |\n| `ci`       | CI/CD workflow changes                            |\n| `chore`    | Dependency bumps, linting, toolchain updates      |\n\n**Scope** is a shortened module path: `LDT/SelfImprovement`, `Quantum`,\n`blueprint`, etc. Omit the `MIPStarRE/` prefix.\n\n### PR body template\n\nEvery PR body must contain three sections:\n\n```markdown\n### Motivation\n- Why this change is needed. Cite the issue and paper/blueprint location.\n\n### Description\n- State precisely what changed.\n\n### Testing\n- What was verified and how (e.g., `lake build`, `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\"`).\n\n---\nAddresses #N\n```\n\nUse `Addresses #N` (keeps the issue open) or `Closes #N` (auto-closes on merge).\n\n### Commit messages\n\n- **Imperative mood** in the subject line (\"Add\", not \"Added\")\n- Subject under 72 characters\n- When squash-merging, the commit message should match the PR title format\n\n## Review Process\n\nEvery PR touching Lean code is reviewed by a dedicated local reviewer session\n(`local/bin/review.sh`, dispatched after green local CI; a session never\nreviews its own diff) against these criteria:\n\n1. **Proof correctness** — No unexplained `sorry`. See `docs/mathematical_language.md`.\n4. **Linter hygiene** — Fix warnings, don't mask them with broad\n   `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks.\n5. **Type safety** — No universe mismatches, coercion problems.\n6. **Performance** — Avoid expensive tactics on large types.\n7. **Modularity** — Are new lemmas general enough to be reused?\n8. **Documentation** — Every new `def` and major This is the **single\nsource of truth** for agent conventions. Claude Code agents should also read\n`CLAUDE.md` for Claude-specific notes.\n\n## Project Overview\n\nThis repository is a Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization project for mathematics\naround $MIP^* = RE$. It is the **local-only continuation** of\n[LionSR/MIPStarRE](https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE): the inherited track is\nthe **low individual degree test (LDT)** paper (arXiv:2009.12982); the active\ntrack is the **quantum Pauli basis test (QPBT)** from *MIP\\*=RE*\n(arXiv:2001.04383, primary) and *NEEXP in MIP\\** (arXiv:1904.05870, secondary).\n\nGitHub is the authority for active issues and pull requests. CI, model-backed\nreview, cache management, and telemetry execute on the local machine and\npublish exact-head evidence through the shared GitHub client. Read\n`local/README.md` and `local/DESIGN.md` before workflow actions.\n\nKey locations:\n\n- `references/qpbt-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of MIP\\*=RE\n  (arXiv:2001.04383); the QPBT lives in\n  `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex` and\n  `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex`\n- `references/neexp-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of NEEXP in MIP\\*\n  (arXiv:1904.05870); secondary source\n  (`07_a_self_test_for_the_pauli_basis.tex`)\n- `references/ldt-paper/` — in-repo TeX source mirror for LDT\n- `blueprint/src/` — active LaTeX blueprint with Lean cross-references\n  (`\\lean{}`, `\\leanok`)\n- `MIPStarRE/` — Lean codebase matching the blueprint\n- `audits/` — dated audit reports, scouting notes, and repair plans\n- `local/`, `results/telemetry/` — local execution and research telemetry\n\nA legacy 2111 tensor track exists under `blueprint/legacy/` — do not modify it.\n\n**Canonical source hierarchy** (use in this order):\n\n1. `references/` paper mirrors — TeX source of the papers\n2. `blueprint/src/chapter/` — active LaTeX blueprint\n3. `MIPStarRE/` — Lean scaffold\n\nAlways read the paper source before formalizing or proving a statement. The\npaper contains the precise mathematical definitions, theorem statements, and\nproof strategies that the Lean code must faithfully represent. When stuck on a\nsorry site or proof, go back to the original paper TeX source — the answer is\nalmost always there. Do not guess or try random tactics without first\nunderstanding the paper's proof strategy.\n\n## Repository Layout\n\n```\nMIPStarRE/\n├── Quantum/               # Reusable matrix / measurement infrastructure\n│   ├── FiniteMatrix.lean  # Op d, normalizedTrace, tauNormSq, IsProj, ...\n│   └── Measurement.lean   # POVM, measurement types\n└── LDT/                   # Low individual degree test (13 submodules)\n    ├── Basic/             # Parameters, operators, distributions, submeasurements\n    ├── Test/              # Test definitions & main theorem\n    ├── Preliminaries/\n    ├── MakingMeasurementsProjective/\n    ├── MainInductionStep/\n    ├── ExpansionHypercubeGraph/\n    ├── GlobalVariance/\n    ├── SelfImprovement/\n    ├── CommutativityPoints/\n    ├── Commutativity/\n    └── Pasting/\n```\n\nEach LDT submodule typically has `Defs.lean` and `Theorems.lean`. Root imports\nflow: `MIPStarRE.lean` → `Quantum` + `LDT` → all submodules.\n\n## Quick Start — Build and Check Commands\n\nRun commands from the repository root unless noted otherwise.\n\n### First-time setup\n\n```bash\nlake exe cache get\nlake build\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check\n```\n\nRun the hook check in every fresh worktree before preparing a PR.  The hooks\nmove fast statement-integrity, proof-debt, changed-file Lean, and blueprint-sync\nchecks to the local workflow so CI is not spent on preventable statement drift.\n\n### Full project build (CI-equivalent)\n\n```bash\nlake build\n```\n\n### Fast single-file type-check (default iteration loop)\n\n```bash\nlake env lean MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in one file\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean || true\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in the whole project\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE\n```\n\n### Declaration checker\n\n```bash\nlake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls\n```\n\nUse this when blueprint declaration lists need to match Lean declarations.\n\n### Blueprint build\n\n```bash\nleanblueprint pdf    # PDF output\nleanblueprint web    # HTML output (use as default for quick checks)\n```\n\nIn CI, blueprint linting effectively runs `leanblueprint web` from `blueprint/`.\n\n### What counts as a single test\n\nThis repository does not have a conventional unit-test suite. The closest\nsingle-test commands are:\n\n- **Lean work**: `lake env lean path/to/File.lean` and\n  `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\" path/to/File.lean || true`\n- **Blueprint work**: `leanblueprint web`\n- **Whole-repo verification**: `lake build` and\n  `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\n\n### Recommended validation sequence\n\nFor a Lean file change:\n\n1. Type-check the edited file with `lake env lean ...`\n2. Scan that file for `sorry|axiom`\n3. If the change affects imports or shared declarations, run `lake build`\n\nFor blueprint changes:\n\n1. Run `leanblueprint web`\n2. If declaration links changed, run `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\n\n## Toolchain\n\n- **Lean**: v4.31.0 (from `lean-toolchain`)\n- **Mathlib**: v4.31.0 (from `lakefile.toml`)\n\nImportant `lakefile.toml` options:\n\n- `relaxedAutoImplicit = false` — declare all variables explicitly\n- `pp.unicode.fun = true`\n- `weak.linter.mathlibStandardSet = true`\n- `maxSynthPendingDepth = 3`\n\n## Proof-Filling Order\n\nSections must be filled in this dependency order:\n\n1. Sections 3–4: test setup and preliminaries\n2. Section 5: making measurements projective\n3. Sections 7–8: expansion and global variance\n4. Section 9: self-improvement\n5. Sections 10–11: commutativity\n6. Section 12: pasting\n7. Section 6: main induction wrapper\n\nDo not start from the final theorem and guess intermediate facts.\n\n## Faithful Formalization Policy\n\nA declaration is a formalization of a paper theorem only when its public Lean\nstatement matches the cited paper statement, up to faithful formal encoding.\nChanging a Lean theorem away from the corresponding statement in\n`references/ldt-paper/` is strongly discouraged and should occur only when a\nfaithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical necessity requires it.\nThis applies to every declaration advertised as a formalization of a paper\nresult, not only to theorems currently undergoing repair.  The check is on the\nhypotheses as well as the conclusion.  A theorem whose\nconclusion has the right shape but whose assumptions include an extra\nload-bearing bridge input or hypotheses bundle is a conditional theorem, not\nthe paper theorem.\nThe project goal is to eliminate such conditional bridges, not to normalize\nthem as permanent infrastructure.\n\nIf the only available Lean theorem has extra assumptions, the blueprint must\nnot mark the source-labelled paper entry as matched by that theorem.  Either\nleave the source-labelled entry without `\\leanok`, or state the restricted or\nconditional result as a separate Lean-only blueprint entry whose hypotheses are\ndisplayed explicitly.  A scope-restricted theorem may be marked `\\leanok` only\nagainst a blueprint statement that explicitly states the restriction; it must\nnot be presented as the unrestricted source theorem.\n\nWhen a stricter-hypothesis Lean theorem is the only available version near a\nsource theorem, the discrepancy must have a paper-gap note or tracking issue.\nThe note should identify the missing hypothesis, explain why it is not part of\nthe cited statement, and state the plan for eliminating the restriction,\nderiving it internally, or moving the result out of the source-labelled route.\n\nThis rule applies especially to declarations named after paper labels such as\n`mainFormal`, `selfImprovement`, `mainInduction`, or other theorem names linked\nfrom the blueprint by `\\lean{...}` and `\\leanok`.\n\nBefore editing any theorem tagged with a paper label (`thm:*`, `lem:*`,\n`prop:*`):\n\n1. Read the corresponding statement in `references/ldt-paper/`.\n2. Preserve the public Lean theorem statement, except for hypotheses that are\n   genuinely part of the faithful encoding of the paper's domain.\n3. Do not add bridge inputs, residual packages, repair hypotheses, producer\n   assumptions, generic hypotheses or assumptions bundles, or arbitrary\n   implication hypotheses to the paper theorem.\n4. If a missing intermediate fact is needed, first state that fact as a named\n   lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.\n5. Do not add a conditional helper merely to keep a file compiling.  A\n   conditional helper may remain temporarily only when the proof content it\n   preserves is mathematically useful, the source-faithful theorem remains\n   visible, and the helper has a paper-gap note, a named construction theorem\n   or proof-obligation target, and an explicit discharge or deletion plan.  Its\n   name must show that it is conditional without making the assumption look like\n   an acceptable source hypothesis, for example\n   `mainFormal_ofInternalObligations`, `selfImprovementFromObligations`, or a\n   name ending in `_ofObligations`.\n6. Do not point a source-labelled blueprint theorem to the conditional helper\n   with `\\leanok`.\n\nWhen reviewing an existing bridge, residual, repair, producer, or package\nhypothesis, first try to recover any genuine proof content from its construction\nand turn that content into a source-faithful lemma.  If the bridge does not\nactually follow from the paper hypotheses, do not preserve the paper theorem as\na strengthened statement.  Restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave\nthe missing proof obligation explicit, even if that means reintroducing a\ntracked `sorry` during a repair PR.\n\nSome side conditions are not deviations: positivity needed to define a\ndivision, nonemptiness of a finite type, decidability instances, field-model\ninstances, and similar boundary hypotheses may be faithful encodings of\nassumptions that the paper leaves implicit.  These should still be reviewed and\ndocumented if they are mathematically load-bearing.  The forbidden pattern is\ndifferent: moving an unproved step of the proof into the theorem statement, such\nas a `BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`,\n`Producer`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic `Assumptions` assumption that the\npaper theorem does not assume.  These assumptions\nshould not be introduced merely to keep a file compiling or to avoid a `sorry`;\nthey require explicit mathematical justification and a planned discharge.\n\nFor the current LDT final theorem, `mainFormal` is reserved for the statement of\n`\\Cref{thm:main-formal}`: from a projective strategy passing the low individual\ndegree test, it produces the three final consistency conclusions.  A theorem\nwith an extra hypothesis such as\n`hbaseBridge : ... → MainFormalRepairedBridgeHypotheses ...` is temporary\nscaffolding at best; it must not be the declaration advertised as\n`thm:main-formal`.  The corresponding paper-aligned version should remain\nvisible, even if its proof is temporarily unfinished during repair.\n\nEvery agent changing a paper-labelled theorem must finish with a statement\nintegrity audit:\n\n- paper assumptions;\n- Lean assumptions;\n- paper conclusion;\n- Lean conclusion;\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\n\n### Paper-realignment mode\n\nWhen a theorem, definition, or hypothesis field has already drifted away from\n`references/ldt-paper/`, a repair PR may temporarily reintroduce `sorry` in\norder to restore the source-faithful statement.  In this mode, statement\nfaithfulness is the first invariant: keeping a divergent proof intact merely to\navoid `sorry` preserves a theorem that the paper does not state.\n\nPaper-realignment mode is narrow.  It applies only to edits whose purpose is to\nremove wrong hypotheses, delete divergent fields, restore a paper theorem\nstatement, or replace a conditional theorem by a paper-facing statement plus a\nnamed proof obligation.  Such a PR must:\n\n1. cite the paper passage by label or line range in the relevant docstring;\n2. cite the paper-gap note or tracking issue that records the divergence;\n3. identify every introduced or retained `sorry` and the construction theorem,\n   proof-obligation theorem, or source-faithful lemma expected to discharge it;\n4. avoid unrelated refactors, notation changes, or proof-engineering churn.\n\nDuring paper realignment, every restated definition, hypothesis field, or\npaper-facing theorem must have a docstring that lets a reviewer tell whether\nthe statement is present in the paper or is a Lean-only proof obligation.  A\nname such as `Bridge`, `Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Input`, or `Producer`\nis not by itself a mathematical source citation.\n\n### Unfaithful dependency markers\n\nA theorem or lemma is **unfaithful** when its proof relies on a hypothesis,\nhelper, bridge, residual, repair input, or conditional theorem that is known not\nto follow from the cited paper statement.  This includes the case where the\npublic theorem statement is source-shaped but the proof calls a conditional\nhelper whose load-bearing hypothesis is not yet derived from the paper\nhypotheses.\n\nSuch a declaration must carry a docstring section beginning with\n`**Unfaithful:**`.  The marker must name the load-bearing deviation, cite the\npaper-gap note or issue that documents it, and state the planned discharge.  A\nminimal form is:\n\n```text\n**Unfaithful:** This proof currently relies on `<hypothesis or helper>`,\nwhich is not derived from `<paper label or line range>`.  Documented in\n`docs/paper-gaps/<note>.tex` or issue `#N`.  Elimination: prove\n`<construction theorem>` from the paper hypotheses.\n```\n\nThe marker propagates through dependencies: a theorem whose proof transitively\nuses an unfaithful declaration is itself unfaithful until the dependency is\nreplaced by a source-faithful proof.  Remove the marker only when the cited\ndeviation has been discharged.\n\nNot every discrepancy requires the full `**Unfaithful:**` marker.  If the paper\nhas a local typo, a documented numerical strengthening, or a genuine scope\nrestriction, use a lighter docstring marker such as `**Local fix:**` or\n`**Scope restriction:**`, citing the relevant paper-gap note.  These lighter\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\npaper hypotheses.\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Imports\n\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\n- One import per line\n- Follow existing local import style\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\n\n### File structure\n\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\n\n1. imports\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\n3. namespace / opens / variables\n4. declarations\n\n### Formatting\n\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\n  own line\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\n  theorem statement\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\n  tactic blocks.\n\n### Naming conventions\n\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\n\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\n\nProject-preferred variable names:\n\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\n- `σ` — strategies\n- `P` — projective measurements\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\n\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\n\n### Types and signatures\n\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\n  wrappers\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\n\n### Documentation\n\nRequired:\n\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\n\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\lean{...}`\nand `\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\n\n## Proof Engineering\n\n### Search before proving\n\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\n\n### Mathlib integration\n\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. When proving lemmas:\n\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\n\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\n\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\n\n### Validation ladder\n\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\n2. `lake build`\n\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\n\n### Lean-specific advice\n\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\n  already in the repo\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\n\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\n\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. Prefer a\nclear, precise, and unhurried expository style: introduce the object under\ndiscussion, state the mathematical relation being used, distinguish hypotheses\nfrom conclusions, and avoid informal process language when a standard\nmathematical phrase is available.\n\nWhen writing docstrings, audit notes, PR descriptions, or blueprint-adjacent\ncomments, use terminology from the standard mathematical literature, the LDT\npaper, and the local formalization. Do not invent slang or private shorthand for\nmathematical objects. The goal is prose that a third-party reader can understand\nwithout having read the agent conversation that produced the change.\n\n### Paper-gap notes\n\nFor the proof-gap terminology used to distinguish source theorems, internal\nproof obligations, and conditional helpers, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.  For documentation of discrepancies\nbetween the cited paper, the blueprint, and Lean, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex`. In particular, such notes should be\nmathematical prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists who have not\nread the issue discussion: introduce notation, state the cited assertion,\nisolate the calculation or logical obstruction, compare with the blueprint and\nLean statement, and give a clear verdict. If Lean uses a Mathlib result or\nconstruction not present in the cited argument, explain that replacement\npedagogically before naming the formal declaration. If the cited assertion is\nfalse and a counterexample is available, explain the counterexample in prose and\nuse any Lean declaration only as verification.\n\n## Proof Integrity\n\n### Blockers (must be resolved before merge)\n\nSee the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md` for the full catalog.\n\n**Direct proof holes**: `sorry`, `admit`\n\n**Kernel / type system bypasses**: `native_decide`, `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce`,\n`lcProof`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`\n\n**Axiom smuggling**: unjustified `axiom` declarations\n\n**Circular reasoning**: proofs that assume the statement being proved as a local\nhypothesis, or helper lemmas that essentially restate the main goal.\n\n**Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)**: custom re-declarations of standard\nMathlib lemmas; `axiom` or `sorry`-based helpers for facts already in Mathlib;\nchains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core.\n\n**Scaffolding that blocks real formalization**: definitions or theorem statements\nthat do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics, making them impossible\nto connect to real Mathlib-based proofs. The short written so its body is the paper's claim, and\na nearby `theorem` restates that claim and proves it by `rfl` (or a one-line\n`simp [foo]` where `foo` is the defining equation). The \"mathematical\ncontent\" has been baked into the definition; the theorem is a tautology. See\nissues [#477], [#494].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\n`rfl` proves that a definition equals itself. If the definition is chosen\n*so that* it equals the conclusion, the `rfl` \"proof\" transports none of the\npaper's reasoning — it is literally the reflexivity of a shape we invented to\nmatch the conclusion. The real identity the paper proves (e.g.,\n`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ` over an actual inner product) is still not stated\nanywhere in Lean.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- A `theorem` whose body is `rfl` / `by rfl` / `by simp [defName]` where\n  `defName` is the def that unfolds to the conclusion.\n- A `structure` with a `Prop`-typed field whose *role* in the paper is a\n  nontrivial identity (SVD, orthonormality, Cauchy–Schwarz), accompanied by a\n  constructor that discharges that field with `rfl`.\n- A `def foo := if α = β then 1 else 0` followed by a theorem asserting\n  `foo α β = if α = β then 1 else 0`.\n- Bridge-like structures where every field is itself a function\n  `(precondition) → (conclusion-step)` and the consumer applies the field\n  directly.\n\n### Concrete example\n\nFrom `MIPStarRE/LDT/ExpansionHypercubeGraph/Defs/Fourier.lean`:\n\n```lean\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\ndef fourierBasisInnerProduct (params : Parameters)\n    (α β : Point params) : Error :=\n  if α = β then 1 else 0\n\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\nlemma fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq (params : Parameters)\n    (α β : Point params) :\n    fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0 := rfl\n\n/-- `prop:eigenvectors`. -/\ntheorem eigenvectors (params : Parameters) :\n    (∀ α β : Point params,\n      fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0) ∧ ... := by\n  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩\n  · intro α β\n    exact fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq params α β    -- castle: def IS Kronecker delta\n  ...\n```\n\nThe paper's orthonormality claim — that the additive characters `φ_α` form an\northonormal basis under the actual inner product\n`⟨f, g⟩ := (1/|V|) · ∑_u f(u)^* · g(u)` — requires a genuine character-sum\nidentity. The Lean theorem states and proves only the trivial fact that the\ndefinition equals itself.\n\n### Not every `rfl` is a castle\n\nDistinguish from legitimate bookkeeping where a named equation is literally\nhow something was defined. Example: `mainFormalError_eq_envelope` in\n`Test/ErrorCascade/Definitions.lean` unfolds the definition of\n`mainFormalError` to its envelope factorization. The mathematical content is\nelsewhere (the envelope is derived from per-step bounds); the `rfl` theorem is\na naming convenience only. The test is: **does the `def` body encode a paper\nidentity, or does it just name a compound expression?**\n\n### How to fix it\n\n1. Move the paper's real definition to the concrete one: for Fourier, define\n   the inner product as the actual sum over vertices, and the characters\n   `φ_α` as functions from `Point params` to `ℂ`.\n2. State the paper's identity (`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ`) as a theorem over those\n   concrete objects.\n3. Prove it via the standard character-sum derivation (or cite the Mathlib\n   counterpart if one exists — `Matrix.dotProduct` / `Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff`\n   combined with `ZMod.sum_pow_units` style lemmas).\n4. If you want to keep the Kronecker shorthand, define it *afterward* as a\n   consequence, not as the primitive.\n\n### Related issues\n\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` field projections (Ch4 SVD as axiom fields)\n- [#494] — the Fourier case and other candidates\n\n---\n\n## A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions\n\n**Smell.** A total function is defined by `if eligible then real_value else\ndefault`, where the `default` (usually `0`, `default`, `⊥`, or\n`Classical.arbitrary`) is a sentinel for \"precondition not met.\" Downstream\ntheorems state properties that are only true on the eligible branch, but the\ntheorem's type signature does not carry the eligibility proof, so the\nobligation moves silently from the prover to whoever happens to call the\nfunction. See issue [#495], related to [#307].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\nThe signature lies about the domain of validity. A caller passing a\nnon-eligible input gets `0` back; any theorem proved about \"the output\" is\nproved for `0`, which is trivially true and carries no information. When a\nlater theorem composes the output with another lemma, the composition\ntype-checks but the conclusion is vacuous on inputs where the original\nprecondition failed.\n\nThe paper, by contrast, restricts the quantifier in the first place:\n\"Fix a tuple `(x₁, ..., x_k)` with Hamming weight `≥ d+1`.\" The Lean should\nmatch.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- `match ... with | some _ => real | none => 0` or `| _ => 0`.\n- `if hEligible : P then ... else default`.\n- Identifier names containing `fallback`, `placeholder`, `sentinel`,\n  `dummy`, `or0`, `orDefault`.\n- Recursive definitions whose base case unconditionally returns a sentinel.\n- Functions that return `Polynomial params` but can return the zero polynomial\n  on inputs that shouldn't be in the domain.\n\n### Concrete example (historical; resolved by PR #561)\n\nUntil PR #561, `MIPStarRE/LDT/Pasting/Defs/Interpolation.lean` contained:\n\n```lean\n/-- Extract the polynomial from a completed slice outcome; returns 0 on ⊥. -/\nnoncomputable def extractSliceOr0 {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]\n    (g : GHatOutcome params) : PolynomialModel params :=\n  match g with\n  | some p => p.poly\n  | none   => 0\n```\n\nThe consumer `interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport` ran Lagrange\ninterpolation on `extractSliceOr0`-extracted values. If the support contained\na `none`, the interpolant silently pretended that slice evaluated to zero.\nThe paper's Lagrange step is quantified over *eligible* slices only, so the\nLean API should carry `∀ i ∈ support, (g i).isSome` as a hypothesis; instead\nit carried nothing, and the theorem technically type-checked on inputs for\nwhich its conclusion was meaningless.\n\n**Current status:** resolved. The live API now removes `extractSliceOr0`,\nthreads the explicit hypothesis `hσsupport : σ ⊆ gHatTupleSupport gs` into\n`interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport`, and packages the chosen support subset\nas `InterpolationSupportWitness` so the arbitrary choice and its proof fields\nare visible at call sites.\n\n### Acceptable uses of this pattern\n\nNot every default branch is a castle. `Inhabited` / `Nonempty` instances\nthat provide a canonical inhabitant (e.g., the zero polynomial for\n`Nonempty (Polynomial params)`) are plumbing, not proof. The test is: **does\nany theorem mention the output?** If a theorem says \"the output satisfies\nP\", and P is not trivially satisfied by the sentinel, the fallback is\nsmuggling a precondition.\n\n### How to fix it\n\nPick one of:\n\n1. **Make the precondition explicit.** Add `(h : eligible input) :` to the\n   signature. Let Lean's type system enforce that non-eligible inputs cannot\n   be passed.\n2. **Return an `Option`.** The `none` result forces every caller to handle\n   the case, so theorems about \"the output\" now quantify only over the\n   `some` branch.\n3. **Restrict the domain.** Instead of `(x : X) → Y`, take `(x : {x : X //\n   P x}) → Y`. Common for finite-support Lagrange-style constructions where\n   the subtype is computable via `Finset.filter`.\n\n### Classical-logic dependencies\n\nA sibling smell in this pattern: `DecidablePred` / `DecidableEq` instances\nthat silently use `Classical.dec` to fill in decidability that should be\nconstructive. The historical `interpolationEligibleSandwichFamily`\nimplementation was exactly such a case: it used `open Classical in ...` to\ngate a predicate that is actually decidable by a finite-support check. Hides real Mathlib gaps. If we decline to use Mathlib because \"our\n   version is simpler,\" the gap never gets filed against Mathlib.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- `private lemma` in a file about well-established algebra/analysis\n  (Cauchy–Schwarz, `sqrt`, `rpow`, `PosSemidef`, `Matrix.trace`, etc.).\n- Custom structures named `MyX` / `LocalX` / `ProjectX` where `X` is a\n  standard concept.\n- Proof bodies that chain ten `private lemma`s where the natural Mathlib\n  counterpart would be two `exact?` lookups.\n- Files with no `import Mathlib.*` above the level of `Mathlib.Tactic.*`\n  when the subject matter is clearly Mathlib-adjacent (linear algebra,\n  analysis, measure theory).\n\n### How to fix it\n\nBefore writing a new lemma, spend one minute on:\n\n- `exact?` / `apply?` on the goal.\n- `#find` / `Loogle` for the statement shape.\n- `rg -n \"theorem.*X\" .lake/packages/mathlib/` for a keyword.\n\nIf Mathlib has it, use it. If it doesn't, consider whether the missing\nlemma should be upstreamed (file an issue against Mathlib, or at least a\nTODO pointing at the gap). The project already has this mandate — see the\n\"Mathlib Integration\" section of [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md):\n\n> Scout Mathlib first (`exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source)\n\nA5 is what happens when that step is skipped.\n\n### Audit cross-reference\n\n`audits/` contains chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency scouting\nreports. If a section of the code review says \"this could use Mathlib\nlemma X\", it belongs in a specific `audits/*.md` file for that chapter.\n\n---\n\n## A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles\n\n**Smell.** A theorem takes a hypothesis of type `SomeStatement` (or\n`SomeWitness`, `SomeOutput`, etc.) that is defined elsewhere and intended\nto represent an external mathematical result, but there is no theorem\nconstructing it from the hypotheses under which the paper uses it. The Lean\nstatement is then:\n\"assuming the external result, the Lean conclusion holds.\" That is\nsometimes legitimate (e.g., a cite to a book whose formalization we don't\nplan to do), and sometimes a cover for locally-unwanted work.\n\nThis overlaps with A1 but is subtler: the hypothesis isn't the\n*current theorem's* conclusion, it's an *independently-named* claim that\nhappens to unblock the current proof.\n\n### Acceptable external smuggles\n\n- **Genuine external citations.** `PolishchukSpielmanClassicalSoundnessStatement`\n  cites the Polishchuk–Spielman theorem; we don't plan to formalize it.\n- **Mathlib gaps we can't fill.** `hMatrixChernoff` in `chernoffBernoulliMatrix`\n  is a Mathlib matrix-Chernoff-type statement; we flagged the gap upstream.\n- **Tracked internal obligations.** A `*Statement` that has an open sub-issue\n  and a named construction theorem target is trackable proof debt. It is still\n  not an acceptable extra hypothesis on a source-labelled paper theorem.\n\n### Unacceptable external smuggles\n\n- A `*Statement` with no open tracking issue, no docstring explaining the\n  mathematical gap, and no consumer-side comment flagging the smuggle.\n- A `*Statement` whose body is the theorem's conclusion, wearing a different\n  name (A1 in disguise).\n- A `*Statement` used to close a lemma whose paper version does not require\n  any such external assumption (silent strengthening of the Lean theorem\n  relative to the paper's).\n\n### How to spot it\n\nGrep for these suffixes: `*Statement`, `*Witness`, `*Claim`,\n`*Conclusion`, `*Output`, `*Input`, `*Hypothesis`, `*Requirement`,\n`*Assumption`, `*Package` (that isn't a `*BridgePackage`). Do not add the structure as a new source-theorem hypothesis\nmerely to keep downstream declarations compiling.\n\n### Merge gate — new `*Statement` / `*Witness` / `*Input` structures\n\nTo prevent dead scaffolds from landing unnoticed (the 5-structure gap of\n2026-04-18–2026-05-08), every PR that introduces a new `structure XStatement`,\n`structure XWitness`, `structure XInput`, `abbrev XStatement`, or\n`abbrev XInput` must satisfy **at least one** of these before merge:\n\n1. **Has a construction theorem.** A theorem that constructs a value of this\n   type from the appropriate paper hypotheses appears in the same PR or an\n   already-merged ancestor. For any theorem or lemma that claims a paper\nresult, ask:\n\n- [ ] **Hypothesis audit.** Does any hypothesis contain (up to `∃`/`∧`) the\n      theorem's conclusion? If yes, that's A1 — reject or strengthen.\n- [ ] **Definitional audit.** Is the proof `rfl` or a one-line `simp`? If\n      yes, does the unfolded definition do the paper's math, or just match\n      the shape of the conclusion? The latter is A2.\n- [ ] **Domain audit.** Does the function have a fallback branch (`if\n      eligible ... else default`)? If yes, does the theorem's signature\n      require eligibility? A lemma that fails one is\nscaffolding, and should be labelled and tracked as such (don't tag with\n`\\leanok` until the gap is closed).\n\n## CI prevention\n\nMechanical detection is possible for many of these patterns:\n\n- **A1 (conclusion-shaped hypothesis).** Use\n  `python3 scripts/audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses.py --ci` as the current\n  report-only tripwire for the PR [#491] inline-existential mutation.      9	This chapter completes the analysis of the Pauli basis test~\cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. Throughout, $(q,m,d)$ is an admissible parameter tuple (Definition~\ref{def:admissible}), $q = 2^t$, and $M = 2^m$ denotes the number of $q$-ary qudits tested for per player. (The letter $M$ also denotes measurement operators, always carrying super- and subscripts; the meaning is determined by context, as in the source.) We fix a projective strategy for the Pauli basis test game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ that succeeds with probability at least $1-\eps$, in the setting of Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-observables}: the shared state $\ket{\psi}$ on registers $\mathrm{A}$, $\mathrm{B}$ is assumed padded with sufficiently many ancilla qubits in the state $\ket{0}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:projective-strategy-setup} and the convention following it), and $\ket{\hat\psi}$ denotes the expanded state on the six registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''$, obtained by adjoining to each player the two halves of $M$ pairs $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ (Definition~\ref{def:expanded-state}). Unless stated otherwise, every $\approx_\delta$ and $\simeq_\delta$ statement below is taken with respect to the state $\ket{\hat\psi}$, over the question distribution named in the statement, with register placements indicated by subscripts; ``all symmetric equivalents'' refers to the register interchanges of Definition~\ref{def:symmetric-equivalents}.

    11	We use the following objects from the preceding chapters: the combined point projectors $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$ acting on the expanded space (Definition~\ref{def:expanded-point-measurement}); the projective polynomial-pair measurement $\{\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}\}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}, with outcomes pairs of polynomials in $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ and error function
    12	\[
    13		\delta_G(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a\bigl(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd}\bigr)
    14	\]
    15	for universal constants $a > 1$, $0 < b < 1$. This is the error denoted $\delta_S$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}; we call it $\delta_G$ here to distinguish the raw global-witness error from the enlarged error used below. We also use the decoding map $\mathrm{Dec} = \mathrm{Dec}_{\F_q}\colon \mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q) \to \F_q^{M}$ of the low-degree code (Definition~\ref{def:decoding-map}, applied with $H = \F_q$; see Remark~\ref{rem:qld-decoding-identity}), which maps a polynomial $g$ to the string of its evaluations on the hypercube $\{0,1\}^m$; and the low-degree encoding $h \mapsto g_h$ together with the vectors $\mathrm{ind}_m(u) \in \F_q^M$, characterized by $h \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u) = g_h(u)$ for all $u \in \F_q^m$ \eqref{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}. We call a polynomial $g \in \mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ an \emph{encoding} if $g = g_h$ for some $h \in \F_q^{M}$ or, equivalently, if $g$ is multilinear; since a multilinear polynomial is determined by its values on $\{0,1\}^m$, the encodings are exactly the $g$ with $g_{\mathrm{Dec}(g)} = g$ as polynomial representatives, and
    16	\[
    17		\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u) = g(u)
    18		\qquad \text{for every encoding $g$ and every } u \in \F_q^m\;.

    27	\begin{remark}[Choice of decoding map and the decoder--encoder identity]\label{rem:qld-decoding-identity}
    28		The source states the constructions of this chapter in terms of its boolean decoding map (the case $H = \{0,1\}$ of Definition~\ref{def:decoding-map}) while describing that map as returning the string of \emph{all} evaluations of $g$ on the hypercube. The proofs require the latter reading, $H = \F_q$, which is adopted throughout this chapter: the linearity of $\mathrm{Dec}$ and the identity $\mathrm{Dec}(g_h) = h$ for all $h \in \F_q^{M}$, both of which fail for the boolean map, are used in the symmetry step of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} and in the conjugation identity \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-6}. The source further asserts the identity $\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u) = g(u)$ for every $g \in \mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$. Since the left-hand side equals $g_{\mathrm{Dec}(g)}(u)$, the identity, taken for all $u \in \F_q^m$, states that the multilinear representative $g_{\mathrm{Dec}(g)}$ and $g$ induce the same function on $\F_q^m$. Every encoding satisfies it, because then $g_{\mathrm{Dec}(g)} = g$ as polynomial representatives; a polynomial that is not an encoding need not: for $m = 1$, $d \geq 2$, and $q > 2$, the polynomial $g(x) = x^2$ has $\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_1(u) = u$, which differs from $g(u) = u^2$ at every $u \notin \{0,1\}$. When $d \leq q-1$ the failure at some $u$ characterizes the polynomials that are not encodings, since evaluation is injective on representatives of individual degree at most $q-1$ (Definition~\ref{def:polynomials-degree}); when $d \geq q$ it does not: for the admissible tuple $(q,m,d) = (8,1,8)$, the polynomial $g(x) = x^8$ is not an encoding, yet $\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_1(u) = u = u^8 = g(u)$ for every $u \in \F_8$. Accordingly, the proofs below invoke the identity only for encodings; in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} the contribution of the remaining outcomes is controlled by the bound \eqref{eq:qld-nonencoding-mass} on the mass that the measurement of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7} places on polynomials that are not encodings, while in the conjugation identity \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-6} the quantity $\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u)$ cancels exactly.

   235		\[
   236			(\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \approx_{O(\delta_G + \eps)} (\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]} \cdot \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{a})_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'}\;.

   239		\[
   240			\E_u \sum_g \bigl\| (\hat{S}^W_{g} \cdot (\Id - \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{g(u)}))_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ket{\hat\psi} \bigr\|^2

   248	\begin{definition}[The swap unitaries]\label{def:v-swap-unitary}

   253		\[
   254			V_{\mathrm{A}} = \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ot \bigl(\tau^X(\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)) \, \tau^Z(\mathrm{Dec}(g_X))\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}''}\;,

   261	\begin{lemma}[Unitarity and conjugation action of the swap unitaries]\label{lem:v-swap-conjugation}
   262		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.swapUnitary_mul_conjTranspose}
   263		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.conjTranspose_mul_swapUnitary}

   268		The maps $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $V_{\mathrm{B}}$ of Definition~\ref{def:v-swap-unitary} are unitaries acting on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$ and $\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''$ respectively, and their conjugation action is exact, as follows. For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, $j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}$, and $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^M$,
   269		\begin{equation}\label{eq:v-swap-obs-conjugation}
   270			V_{\mathrm{A}} \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger = \Id_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ot \bigl( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \bigr)_{\mathrm{A}''}
   271			\qquad \text{and} \qquad
   272			V_{\mathrm{B}} \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_{\mathrm{B}}^\dagger = \Id_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot \bigl( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \bigr)_{\mathrm{B}''}\;,
   273		\end{equation}
   274		and for all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, $u \in \F_q^m$, and $a \in \F_q$,
   275		\begin{equation}\label{eq:qld-unitary-6}
   276			V_{\mathrm{B}} \, \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a \, V_{\mathrm{B}}^\dagger = \Id_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot (\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\mathrm{B}''}\;,
   277			\qquad
   278			\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \sum_{h \,:\, g_h(u) = a} \tau^W_h\;,
   279		\end{equation}
   280		together with the analogous identity for $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$.
   281	\end{lemma}
   282	\begin{proof}
   283		\uses{lem:qld-4-7, lem:tildew-product-form, lem:twisted-commutation, def:v-swap-unitary, def:tilde-m-measurement, def:tau-dot-product-projector, def:indicator-vector, def:decoding-map, def:generalized-pauli}
   284		Since the measurement $\{\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}\}$ is projective (Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}) and the $\tau^X, \tau^Z$ observables are self-inverse,
   285		\[
   286			V_{\mathrm{A}} V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger = \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ot \Id_{\mathrm{A}''} = \Id_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''}\;,
   287		\]
   288		and the same computation gives $V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger V_{\mathrm{A}} = \Id$, so $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ is unitary; likewise $V_{\mathrm{B}}$. For \eqref{eq:v-swap-obs-conjugation}, conjugate the product form \eqref{eq:tildewj-product-form} of $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:tildew-product-form}): by the orthogonality of the projectors $\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}$, only the diagonal terms survive, and the twisted commutation relation (Lemma~\ref{lem:twisted-commutation})
   289		\[
   290			\tau^X(\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)) \, \tau^Z(\mathrm{Dec}(g_X)) \, \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = (-1)^{\tr( e_j(\mathrm{Dec}(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \, \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \, \tau^X(\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)) \, \tau^Z(\mathrm{Dec}(g_X))
   291		\]
   292		cancels the sign $(-1)^{\tr(e_j (\mathrm{Dec}(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))}$ term by term, leaving $\sum_{g_X,g_Z} \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z} \ot \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = \Id \ot \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u})$. Substituting $h' = h + \mathrm{Dec}(g)$ turns the constraint $h \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u) = (\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u)) - a$ into $h' \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u) = -a = a$, since $\F_q$ has characteristic $2$; the quantity $\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u)$ cancels exactly, so no relation between it and $g(u)$ is used (Remark~\ref{rem:qld-decoding-identity}).    293	\end{proof}

   295	\begin{lemma}[Extraction of the EPR state and the Pauli observables]\label{lem:qld-unitary}
   296		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ExtractionWitness}

   300		There exists a function $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$, where $\delta_P = C(\delta_G + \sqrt{\eps} + md/q)$ is the construction error above, and there exist unitaries $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ acting on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$ and $V_{\mathrm{B}}$ acting on registers $\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''$, such that the following hold.
   301		\begin{enumerate}
   302			\item There exists a state $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}$ on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'$ such that
   303			\[
   304				\bigl\| V_{\mathrm{A}} \ot V_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''} - \ket{\mathrm{aux}}_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}''} \bigr\|^2 \leq \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}\;.
   305			\]
   306			\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
   307			\begin{align*}
   308				V_{\mathrm{A}} \, \bigl(M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h \bigr)_{\mathrm{A}} \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}} \Id_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ot (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''}\;, \\
   309				V_{\mathrm{B}} \, \bigl(M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h \bigr)_{\mathrm{B}} \, V_{\mathrm{B}}^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}} \Id_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{B}''}\;,
   310			\end{align*}
   311			where the $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}''}$, with the answer summation over $h \in \F_q^{M}$ and no average over questions.
   312		\end{enumerate}

   315	\begin{proof}
   316		\uses{def:v-swap-unitary, lem:v-swap-conjugation, lem:tildew-product-form, lem:qld-construct-the-paulis, lem:qld-win-implications, fact:triangle-for-simeq, def:bracket, lem:cancellation, lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree, lem:qld-4-7}
   317		For the first item, the self-consistency of the observables $\tilde{W}^j$ (Item~2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}) is equivalent, since these observables are Hermitian involutions (Lemma~\ref{lem:tildew-product-form}), to $\E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^M} \bra{\hat\psi} \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ot \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ket{\hat\psi} \geq 1 - \delta_P/2$; setting $\ket{\vartheta} = V_{\mathrm{A}} \ot V_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\hat\psi}$ and using the exact conjugation identities of Lemma~\ref{lem:v-swap-conjugation}, this becomes $\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - \delta_P/2$ for $W \in \{X,Z\}$, where $H_W = \E_j \E_{\tilde{u}} \, \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \ot \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = \bigl( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(s) \ot \tau^W(s) \bigr)^{\ot M}$ by the tensor factorization of $\tau^W(\tilde{u})$ and the invariance of the uniform average over $s$ under $s \mapsto e_j s$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:cancellation}, $\E_{s,s'} \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') \ot \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') = \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ on each pair of qudits, whence $H_X H_Z = \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$.    318		% Case distinction added: the source normalizes the projected vector
   319		% without ensuring that it is nonzero; see Remark rem:qld-unitary-triangle-slip.
   320		If $\delta_P > 1/8$, then, after enlarging the universal constant in $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$, both items of the lemma hold with $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}$ an arbitrary unit state, since their left-hand sides never exceed $4$; assume therefore $\delta_P \leq 1/8$. Then the vector $(\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M})_{\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\vartheta}$ has squared norm at least $1 - 4\delta_P \geq 1/2 > 0$, and $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}$ may be defined as its normalization; the overlap of $\ket{\vartheta}$ with $\ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$ equals the norm of that vector and is at least $\sqrt{1 - 4\delta_P} \geq 1 - 4\delta_P$, which yields the first item with a bound of $8\delta_P = O(\sqrt{\delta_P})$. For the second item, Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} gives, on average over $u \in \F_q^m$, $M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \ot \Id \simeq_\eps \Id \ot M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$ and $\Id \ot M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \simeq_\eps M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \ot \Id$, where $M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h$; combining these with Item~1 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} by Lemma~\ref{fact:triangle-for-simeq}, using $\eps \leq \sqrt{\eps} \leq \delta_P$, yields $M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \ot \Id \simeq_{\sqrt{\delta_P}} \Id \ot \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a$. Writing $\ket{\Delta} = \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$, the quantity to be bounded for the $\mathrm{A}$-side relation equals $2 - 2\sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_{\mathrm{A}} M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger \ot (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\Delta}$, since $(\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''} \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M} = (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$. Replacing $(\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{B}''}$ by the averaged coarse-graining $\E_u \sum_{h' : g_{h'}(u) = g_h(u)} (\tau^W_{h'})_{\mathrm{B}''}$ costs at most $md/q$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree} (distinct $h \neq h'$ have distinct encodings $g_h \neq g_{h'}$, of total degree at most $md$), and by \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-6} the resulting sum equals $\E_u \sum_{a} \bra{\Delta} V_{\mathrm{A}} M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger \ot V_{\mathrm{B}} \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a V_{\mathrm{B}}^\dagger \ket{\Delta}$. Exchanging $\ket{\Delta}$ for $\ket{\vartheta}$ costs $O(\delta_P^{1/4})$ by the first item, and the resulting expression $\E_u \sum_a \bra{\hat\psi} M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \ot \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat\psi}$ is at least $1 - O(\sqrt{\delta_P})$ by the $\simeq_{\sqrt{\delta_P}}$ relation above. Altogether the distance is $O(\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$; the $\mathrm{B}$-side relation is proved identically.
   321	\end{proof}

   323	\begin{remark}[Two steps in the source proof of the extraction lemma]\label{rem:qld-unitary-triangle-slip}
   324		In the source proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary}, the triangle inequality gives $\| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \| \leq \| (\Id - H_X)\ket{\vartheta} \| + \| (\Id - H_Z)\ket{\vartheta} \| \leq 2\sqrt{\delta_P}$, so that $\| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \leq 4\delta_P$; the source instead asserts the bound $2\sqrt{\delta_P}$ for the \emph{squared} norm, which holds only when $\sqrt{\delta_P} \leq 1/2$, and consequently carries the term $\sqrt{\delta_P}$ into an overlap bound of $1 - 2\delta_P - \sqrt{\delta_P}$. The proof above uses the corrected bound $4\delta_P$, which gives the overlap bound $1 - 4\delta_P$ and leaves the final bound $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}} = O(\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$ unchanged. The source proof also normalizes the vector $(\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M})_{\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\vartheta}$ without ensuring that it is nonzero; the case distinction on $\delta_P$ in the proof above supplies this, the conclusions of the lemma being trivial when $\delta_P$ exceeds a universal constant.
   325	\end{remark}
